items.followUp: Why are viruses called obligate intracellular parasites?

rubric.why: Explains the absence of cellular structure that makes viruses acellular.
rubric.description: Viruses lack cellular organization and are not made of cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses are not made of cells or lack cellular organization.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic non-cellular components of a virus.
rubric.description: A virus consists of nucleic acid enclosed in a protein coat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the nucleic acid and the protein coat.

modelAnswer: Viruses are called acellular because they lack cellular organization and are not made of cells.
A virus consists of nucleic acid enclosed in a protein coat, rather than the structures of a cell.

items.followUp: What is the function of the plasma membrane?

rubric.why: Recognizes that the terms refer to one structure, not two different membranes.
rubric.description: Plasma membrane and cell membrane are two names for the same structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the terms refer to the same membrane or structure.

rubric.why: Gives a correct location or property of the membrane.
rubric.description: The membrane surrounds the protoplasm and is selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either its location around the protoplasm or its selective permeability.

modelAnswer: Plasma membrane and cell membrane are two names for the same structure; they are not different membranes.
The membrane surrounds the protoplasm and is selectively permeable.

items.followUp: What happens to the reaction rate when substrate is added after an enzyme’s active sites are saturated?

rubric.why: Defines saturation by stating that substrate occupies all enzyme active sites.
rubric.description: Saturation occurs when all enzyme active sites are occupied by substrate molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all active sites are occupied by substrate.

rubric.why: States the effect of saturation on the reaction rate.
rubric.description: At saturation the reaction rate reaches its maximum and does not increase further when more substrate is added.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate is maximal or does not increase further.

modelAnswer: Saturation of active sites occurs when all the active sites of enzyme molecules are occupied by substrate molecules.
The reaction rate then reaches its maximum and does not increase further when more substrate is added.
